fields.title: Make hook-fired writes always target the real database
fields.description: Make hook-fired writes, such as session registration, events and task status changes, always target the real database even inside a sandboxed worktree.
fields.context: After E-1426 retired companion files, the sessions table is ground truth for Claude-pane registration.
fields.analysis:
## Known limitation: deferred to E-1458 (2026-05-23)

E-1450's "all hook-fired writes go to the real DB" rule is correct for production but unconditional — it leaves no affordance for legitimate self_dev testing scenarios where a developer wants to exercise the hook binaries (the 5-10 separate Go apps per E-893 / E-1367 fan-out) against a sandbox DB without polluting the real ledger.

Implement E-1450 as designed. The current edge-case carve-outs in the prompt (test-fixture detection, sandbox-init bypass) are stand-ins, not a full solution. When hook testing against the sandbox becomes a felt need, **E-1458** ("Allow opt-in hook routing to sandbox DB for self_dev testing") addresses it properly — an opt-in mechanism (env var, per-event marker, or wrapper) that bypasses the IsSandboxActive() override at the hook entry.

Until E-1458 lands, hook tests must either inject DB handles explicitly or accept that hook events leak to the real DB.

## From the description

Fix: ALL hook-fired writes (session registration, event emission, task-status transitions) target the real DB regardless of sandbox routing,

because these reflect real-world activity not test fixture data.

Rare edge cases can be carved out individually.

fields.title: Fix migrate-db dry run applying migrations
fields.description: Fix the migrate-db dry run so it reports pending migrations without applying them, instead of auto-migrating on open and then claiming everything was already applied.
fields.context:
cmd/endless-event main.go calls monitor.DB() to get the connection;

DB() unconditionally invokes migrate(db, MigrateOpts{Runner: RunnerAuto}) before main.go reads -dry-run.

So the real migration runs, then the dry-run code path reports everything 'already applied' — misleading no-op.

Discovered during E-1396 when a -dry-run command actually applied V11 to the real DB.
fields.analysis: Fix needs to either split DB-open from auto-migrate, plumb a dry-run signal into DB(), or deprecate the flag as a footgun.

fields.title: Fix the rebuild-required migration gate breaking fresh DBs
fields.description: Fix the gate on migrations that require a rebuild so fresh databases, such as tests and new installs, can pass it instead of being refused.
fields.context:
When a registered migration sets RequiresRebuild: true, internal/monitor/migrate.go returns ErrRequiresRebuild and refuses to advance the schema unless opts.AllowRebuild is set.

Discovered during E-1396 when adding the flag on V11 broke 53 fresh-DB tests immediately, forcing me to drop the flag and rely on BEGIN IMMEDIATE TRANSACTION alone.

The flag is currently unused on main but the next user who needs it will hit the same wall — and worse, can't ship it at all without breaking every fresh install.
fields.analysis: Fix needs an escape hatch: either auto-skip when the rebuild would be a no-op (introspect target shape), or distinguish 'fresh DB created this version' from 'existing DB needs operator approval to rebuild'.

fields.title: Identify the current Claude pane from its environment
fields.description: Identify the current Claude pane from the environment variables Claude Code sets instead of a database lookup, keeping the database for finding sibling panes.
fields.notes:
After E-1450 lands (hook-fired writes always target the real DB), the dominant cause of attribution failure goes away — the cross-DB sandbox vs real-DB confusion that motivated E-1455's original framing.

Composes with E-1450 (does not replace it).

Originally framed during E-1396 verification; re-scoped after discovering E-1450 already addresses the cross-DB issue.
fields.context:
What remains is detection-side: session_id_resolve() identifies a Claude pane by querying the DB for a matching row, not by reading the env vars Claude Code already exposes (CLAUDECODE=1, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, TMUX_PANE).

This leaves a first-event-timing race (CLI runs before the first hook event has registered the pane in the DB) and unnecessary DB round-trips for current-pane identification.
